subject: Clarifying activation triggers and billing start for AWS Marketplace fulfillment
messages:
From: Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying activation triggers for AWS Marketplace fulfillment & metering

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited about accelerating the integration. Before legal and procurement sign off we need to lock down exactly when entitlement "activates" for billing and metering purposes in the contract. On past marketplace listings we've run into ambiguity and downstream invoicing disputes, so procurement asked that we produce a short matrix that answers: 

- Which event constitutes activation for billing start? (AWS entitlement grant, first API call, customer seat provisioning in our app)
- When does metering begin (first metering event submitted to MPX, first invoiceable unit)?
- Who is responsible for issuing the entitlement on the marketplace side vs our side?
- Fallbacks: if usage reporting lags or webhook delivery fails, how are corrections/backfills handled?

Can you send a one-page matrix and confirm whether Redwood requires the DocuSign contract to be completed before AWS entitlement is issued or if AWS can be used to trigger entitlement (we prefer entitlement only after signed contract, but want to understand options). Attached is a draft Excel with our procurement fields.

Thanks — we need this clarified by end of next week to keep our procurement window open.

Sarah Wells
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Health
[sent from mobile]

Attachment: MPX_Activation_Draft.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying activation triggers for AWS Marketplace fulfillment & metering

Hi Sarah — really appreciate the clear list. We put together a proposed activation & metering matrix (attached) that maps contract language, marketplace entitlement events, and our recommended operational defaults. High-level summary below: 

- Billing start: Default = entitlement provisioning in AWS Marketplace (seller-initiated on our side) but we can change to "contract signature" if Acme requires entitlement only post-DocuSign.
- Metering begin: First successful metering event accepted by AWS Marketplace (we send usage events). We support backfill within 60 days for delivery failures; any backfilled tokens are reconciled on next invoice cycle.
- Responsibility: Redwood issues the entitlement on AWS once contract countersigned OR upon receiving signed PO + DocuSign confirmation; procurement preference will determine which triggers first.
- Failover/backfill: If webhook or metering ingestion fails, our recommended path is: (1) send secure usage report via S3/CSV, (2) Redwood triggers manual reconciliation and applies a back-dated invoice credit if needed.

If Acme prefers "billing start = DocuSign executed", we will add that clause to the SOW and coordinate a DocuSign webhook to trigger our entitlement flow. If you want entitlement immediately after purchase through AWS (faster time-to-value), we will require a payment guarantee (PO or credit card) and a separate cancellation window.

I've attached Redwood_MPX_Activation_Matrix_v1.xlsx. Can we sync Thursday 4/15 for 30 minutes to confirm which option Acme prefers? If you confirm "contract first" we'll prepare the exact clause language for legal.

— Mina
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MPX_Activation_Matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying activation triggers for AWS Marketplace fulfillment & metering

On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 11:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I've attached Redwood_MPX_Activation_Matrix_v1.xlsx. Can we sync Thursday 4/15 for 30 minutes to confirm which option Acme prefers? If you confirm "contract first" we'll prepare the exact clause language for legal.

Agree with Mina's defaults. A couple of practical notes from ops: 

- For "entitlement = AWS provisioning" we need an automated DocuSign webhook or a signed PO deposit for high-value deals to avoid unpaid usage exposure.
- Add a clear SLA for usage-event delivery: 99.5% webhook success; if below that threshold over a billing month, Redwood will accept responsibility for manual ingestion/backfill within 30 days and will not apply penalties to customer. 
- Recommend a clause that allows a single retroactive reconciliation (backfill) window of 60 days and then audit-only adjustments thereafter.

I'll draft the legal-friendly clause and loop Jonas for pricing impact (proration, free trial credit treatment). Aditya, can you validate that our current metering pipeline supports a 60-day backfill and S3 CSV ingestion?

Marissa
Director, Marketplace Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying activation triggers for AWS Marketplace fulfillment & metering

Thanks — we've reviewed the matrix and procurement is leaning toward: billing start = DocuSign-executed contract OR receipt of signed PO (whichever comes first). That covers our internal controls. Two asks before we can sign: 

1) Add an explicit statement that any backfilled usage > $5k requires prior notice and approval from Acme procurement.
2) Payment terms: standard Net30 is preferred. Can Redwood accept Net30 for this deal? If not, we need a short justification for Net15 or prepay.

If you can include those two items in the clause language we'll circulate to legal. HubSpot link to our deal is here: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/HS-98765.

Sarah
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Health
Attachment: ACME_PO_45321.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 10:16 AM Sarah Wells <sarah.wells@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks — we've reviewed the matrix and procurement is leaning toward: billing start = DocuSign-executed contract OR receipt of signed PO (whichever comes first). That covers our internal controls. Two asks before we can sign:
>
> 1) Add an explicit statement that any backfilled usage > $5k requires prior notice and approval from Acme procurement.
> 2) Payment terms: standard Net30 is preferred. Can Redwood accept Net30 for this deal?

Hi Sarah — we can accommodate both asks. Plan: 

- Clause language: "Billing commencement shall be the earlier of Redwood's receipt of a countersigned DocuSign agreement or the Customer's signed purchase order. Any backfill adjustments to billed usage exceeding $5,000 USD shall be subject to prior written notice to the Customer and approval from Customer procurement prior to invoicing."
- Payment terms: Redwood agrees to Net30 for this specific deal (Deal ID RDW-ACME-2027-05). We'll flag finance for the commercial credit check; Jonas is agreeable.
- Ops follow-up: Aditya will configure the entitlement flow to require a DocuSign webhook or PO upload to the marketplace entitlement console for this account and enable 60-day backfill with manual approval required for > $5k.

Next steps: I'll draft the SOW clause and send to your legal with our proposed language and the updated activation matrix. Target: send by EOD 4/21 so Acme legal has time to review before their procurement window closes.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
